source_caption:
The Marvel show for people who don’t like Marvel.

Meanwhile, the iconic hallway fight scene in Marvel's Daredevil is celebrated as a pinnacle of TV action because it prioritizes visceral exhaustion, practical stunt work, and grounded realism over polished, superhuman choreography.Its realism stems from several deliberate creative choices. Unlike typical action heroes who fight endlessly without tiring, Matt Murdock gets visibly winded. He leans on walls to catch his breath, stumbles, and drags his feet. The actor, Charlie Cox, and the stunt team performed the grueling sequence until they were genuinely exhausted, which translates to a highly authentic on-screen performance. 

Special acknowledgment to the sequence's stunt coordinator and fight choreographer, Philip J Silvera, for masterminding the physical layout and realistic execution of this landmark television sequence.

source_details.title: Daredevil
source_details.synopsis: Marvel's Daredevil is an American television series created by Drew Goddard for the streaming service Netflix, based on the Marvel Comics character Daredevil. It is set in the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU), sharing continuity with the films of the franchise, and was the first Marvel Netflix series leading to the crossover miniseries The Defenders (2017). Daredevil was produced by Marvel Television in association with ABC Studios. Steven S. DeKnight served as showrunner for the first season, with Doug Petrie and Marco Ramirez taking over as co-showrunners for the second, and Erik Oleson joining the series as showrunner for the third; Goddard served as a consultant for the series.
